title: Just Epic Dimensions 2.0.0 playable showcase
kind: Human-readable index; install the individual files under config/

dimensions.name: Showcase Hub
features: Creative mode while visiting; previous normal mode restores on exit
One-time centered spawn structure placement, including block states and working block entities
Independent 512-block border centered on spawn
Radius-1 retained spawn chunks with continuous empty-dimension ticking
Paused noon clock and custom sky
Expanded labelled demonstration stations and tour book
Operator monitoring station: in-game diagnostics and client-linked browser dashboard
notes: Start here using /tpj; this bundle does not change the normal initial spawn dimension.
The furnace contains eight raw iron and coal. Visit another dimension and return to see smelting continue.
Only the hub stays loaded; spawnChunkRadius is 0 in the other showcases.
The showcase hub explicitly enables monitoring history; global monitoring remains unchanged.
Showcase installation does not grant operator permissions or change initial player placement.

dimensions.name: Prismatic Meadow
features: Flower-forest terrain with its own seed
Mint grass, teal foliage, lavender water, pink clouds and a larger tinted sun
Bounded repeating afternoon clock and a limited celestial arc
Sky travel above Y=224 returns to the hub, including passengers
Irregular weighted flower-forest, meadow and cherry-grove regions
Repeated biome-restricted open pavilions with outdoor cooking, workstations and food gardens
notes: Native foliage blending and client Clouds/color settings still apply.
Fly upward or use /tp @s ~ 230 ~ to try the sky return.
Sun position and raw clock are separate controls; repeating this window keeps the same calendar day.
Use the worldgen biome map at this dimension seed to inspect the distribution before generating more chunks.
Pavilion placement uses spacing 10 and separation 4; cherry pavilions only generate in cherry groves.

dimensions.name: Crimson Nightmare
features: Extreme dimension-only biome tints: vivid red grass, pitch-black biome-tinted leaves and violet water
Fixed dark-purple Overworld sky and a four-times-size orange-red sun; moon, stars and sunrise gradient hidden
Fixed acid-green clouds at Y=96 and fixed green fog from 4 to 160 blocks with cylindrical distance
Paused late-afternoon clock (11000) preserves the sun composition; native Nether music with a 1–3 second selection delay
Independent Overworld noise terrain and seed using jungle vegetation, without generated structures or natural mob spawning
notes: This is an appearance showcase; its threatening atmosphere does not enable hostile spawning or hardcore.
The palette affects this dimension only. Biome-tinted grass and oak/jungle foliage change; fixed-color texture details retain their own colors.
Clouds must be enabled in Minecraft, and enableColorOverrides must be enabled in the JED client config.

dimensions.name: Long-Day Wilderness
features: Normal multinoise Overworld biomes and structures with an independent generation seed
JED custom 36000-tick day / 6000-tick night cycle
Friendly natural spawning enabled while hostile natural spawning is disabled
Independent weather; natural lightning disabled
Wildlife observation deck with wolves, foxes, cows, chickens and pigs excluded from natural and initial-generation spawning
Sheep weights increased; sheep dimension/player caps and added rabbit entries
notes: At normal clock speed the combined cycle is 35 real minutes, without changing simulation speed.
/jed seed justepicdimensions:showcase_long_day reports this dimension’s effective seed.
Named time commands keep Minecraft’s raw values; they are not rescaled to the custom cycle.
Rules cover natural spawning and initial chunk-generation animals. Other types, including modded creatures, remain eligible. Existing animals and deliberate spawn eggs are not removed or blocked.
The 240-loaded and 48-within-48-block limits count sheep only. Minecraft's separate shared creature cap still applies, so other creatures can prevent further natural sheep spawning.
Native placement, light, biome checks and mob caps still apply; additions are opportunities, not forced spawns.

dimensions.name: Frost Garden
features: Snowy-plains terrain and persistent snow weather
Snow can accumulate while water freezing is independently disabled
Sleep is allowed and does not clear the weather
Cold sky/cloud/fog colors
Survival expedition lodge with sheltered and exposed testing areas
Sky-exposed snowfall applies Slowness and periodic freezing damage
Vanilla and MPS Re-modularized Power Armor boots/leggings reduce direct hazard damage; their chestplates suppress the complete rule
notes: Starts at a paused nighttime so a bed can demonstrate weather retention. With doDaylightCycle=false, sleeping does not advance the clock.
Disabling ice creation does not remove ice already generated by a terrain feature.
Snow accumulates through native ticking; JED does not blanket-repaint existing terrain.
Take food and protective gear before leaving the roof. Boots reduce damage 25%, leggings 50%; strongest item wins.
Vanilla and all four MPS Power Armor tiers use the same equipped-slot rules. Their chestplates grant full protection against this showcase rule; lingering Slowness expires normally.

dimensions.name: Lantern Cavern
features: Enclosed lush cavern with no skylight and a custom dimension type
16-entry brightness table, full-chunk/update light verification and dark fog
Beds save checkpoints but cannot be used to sleep
8:1 coordinate scale; void travel returns to the hub using native dimension scaling
Rolling moss-covered terrain, shallow pools and an uneven stone ceiling
Native lush-cave vegetation and dense glow-berry canopies
Lush lower and dripstone upper biome bands
Illuminated gardens, ceiling-hanging ruins and a signed bed checkpoint
notes: Sleeping is explicitly denied. Beds are checkpoints only: a valid bed can save a respawn point, but cannot start sleep or skip night.
No skylight, mossy slopes and an uneven stone ceiling make the custom brightness and lamp-light contrast visible.
Clocks/ordinary compasses retain non-surface behavior. Water placement does not evaporate.
/tpj justepicdimensions:showcase_cavern 20 -12 20 tests the void return near hub X/Z 160.
Terrain and decoration use native noise settings and normal biome features; no flat grass/deepslate chamber.
Inspect biome IDs below and above Y=80; ordinary bed sleep remains denied.

dimensions.name: Loadout Arena
features: Separate inventory group and forced Survival mode
First-entry kit plus a smaller respawn kit; native hotbar, armor and offhand containers
Nighttime hostile natural spawning, Hard difficulty and no friendly natural spawning
Independent 128-block border, denied bed checkpoints, and death routing back into the arena
A carried hub key unlocks entry; /tpj list shows a locked destination without it
Independent XP, capped health, absorption, food and paused effect snapshots
Natural zombies, skeletons and spiders with population caps
Personal arena instances with each configured category scoped per instance
notes: Your original inventory/Ender Chest/accessory state returns on leaving this group. Existing arena gear is restored on re-entry.
Death drops arena gear. Installed grave integrations may suppress the respawn kit when gear is recoverable; that is intentional.
Use /tpj justepicdimensions:showcase_hub spawn to leave. This dimension is permanent, not reset on exit.
Take a tripwire-hook Arena Key from the hub before ordinary entry. It is checked in the departing inventory, before arena gear loads.
Leave, change your ordinary state, then return: saved arena values restore independently. Same-group death still follows native death rules.
Operators: /tpj instance create justepicdimensions:showcase_arena, then enter the returned instance ID; exit returns through the authorized entry/fallback route.

dimensions.name: Temporary Quarry
features: Layered resource terrain with a native flat generator
Temporary lifecycle with automatic idle unload after 30 seconds of eligibility
World files reset through the temporary-dimension lifecycle
Shares the ordinary inventory group so mined items can be brought back
notes: TEMPORARY: blocks, chests, builds and loose items here are disposable. Bring out anything you want to keep.
After everybody leaves, tickets/active work must drain before the 30-second idle close/reset can happen.
Shutdown also cleans a loaded temporary dimension. Forced chunks can postpone ordinary idle unloading.

dimensions.name: Pillarless End
features: Independent End terrain seed and native dragon fight data
No naturally generated spike pillars and no pillar reconstruction during crystal resummoning
Forced Creative observation, local border, purple fog and End music
End provider retains native End-return behavior
notes: A native dragon fight is enabled; Creative mode is for observing it.
This is a separate dimension and does not alter minecraft:the_end.
Native exit portals retain End-return behavior; /tpj can always return you to the hub.

dimensions.name: Team Loadout Arena
features: Team-owned arena runs with current scoreboard-team membership
Per-player snapshots isolated per instance; membership loss uses the existing secure evacuation
notes: Operators: /team add showcase_blue; /team join showcase_blue <player>; /tpj instance create justepicdimensions:showcase_team_arena
Use /tpj instance enter <id>; build a marker, exit, and compare with another authorized personal/team run. No automatic world creation or relaxed command permissions.

dimensions.name: Scheduled Quarry
features: Persistent resource terrain with a 15-minute real-time recurring reset
Due resets defer while occupied and block ordinary arrivals; normal idle unloading saves terrain
When useShowcase and Chunky are present, bounded preparation automatically runs initially and after reset
notes: DISPOSABLE: carry mined items out. A due reset waits until empty; the lifecycle fallback is the hub. Scheduled history is retained seven days.
Without Chunky this quarry stays usable. With Chunky, /jed pregen status justepicdimensions:showcase_scheduled_quarry reports readiness.
Optional pregeneration is supplied in memory when useShowcase is enabled; an explicit pregeneration field in the installed properties takes precedence.
